title: Qwen 3-8 B on HypoSpace
body: Valid-outcome coverage and reasoning efficiency
GAPO, process distillation, and preliminary MS-TTRL
notes: Our task has multiple correct answers. Producing one correct answer repeatedly is therefore insufficient: the model must recover different valid mechanisms. We investigated inference settings, group-aware rewards, reasoning distillation, and self-verification. Our main case study is the first held-out 36-task confirmation. Outputs became substantially shorter, while coverage improved numerically but not conclusively. We also report the attempts that did not help and the later tests that limit our conclusions.

title: Validity, repetition, and coverage
body: Finite observations can admit several valid mechanisms
Complete GT → parsing → canonicalization → scoring
GT={A, B, C}; samples=A, A, A, A: VR=100%, RR=1/3
table: Definition in our later IID protocol
Distinct parseable outcomes / N; errors may count
Distinct valid mechanisms / complete GT size
notes: HypoSpace constructs observations and exhaustively enumerates compatible mechanisms. We use causal graphs, 3 D structures, and Boolean expressions. Suppose the valid set contains A, B, and C. Four copies of A achieve perfect validity but recover only one-third of the set. NR measures distinct parseable outcomes, and can increase because of different wrong answers; RR is therefore essential. We separate task families before building multiple training answers, and compare models on the same tasks and budgets. Mechanism identity also matters: logical equivalence is not always the benchmark’s definition of the same Boolean mechanism.
source: HypoSpace repository; strict GT scorer src/reward.py

title: Thinking helps; default DSH does not reliably help
body: Eight conditions: 8B/27B × thinking × direct/DSH
Early small tasks and N=GT; not comparable to later N=4
Successful DSH candidates usually took one model step
notes: We first worried that an 8 B model would score too poorly to distinguish methods. The eight-condition comparison showed meaningful headroom once thinking was enabled. The default DSH wrapper did not consistently improve recovery, and successful candidates usually involved only one model step. That constrains this wrapper configuration, not all iterative search methods. These early tests used smaller tasks, history-conditioned generation, andN equal to ground-truth multiplicity. Later absolute scores must not be compared directly. This baseline motivated continuing with 8 B rather than simply switching to a larger model. SpeakerB will now explain the reward-based attempts.

title: GAPO works on lists; transfer remains limited
body: Reward low-frequency valid outcomes within a group
List: BF16/G32/200 updates; Hypo: NF4/G8/40 updates
Hypothesis: reward reweighting cannot create unseen support
notes: GAPO makes rewards depend on the frequency of valid outcomes within a group. In our teammate’s list-task replication, all three training seeds increased the number of distinct valid answers. This is positive evidence that the mechanism can reshape an output distribution. Direct transfer to our harder HypoSpace setup did not beat Base: RR was 18.74 versus 18.77. There were only three independent test tasks per domain, so this is a narrow result. One possible limitation is support: rewards can reweight answers that appear, but cannot automatically teach reasoning for valid mechanisms never sampled.

title: MS-TTRL: higher validity, no coverage advantage yet
body: Same-policy verification + cache + rare-outcome rewards
One seed, two domains; formal 3D evaluation pending
Training cost: 5.6–10.1× the majority baseline
notes: MS-TTRL separates correctness estimation from generation frequency. The policy verifies candidate outcomes, while frequency promotes rare reliable solutions. Our teammate has a preliminary comparison at epoch 10, seed 1337, on 18 Boolean and causal tasks. MS-TTRL has the highest validity, but its recovery does not beat Base, and majority TTRL has the best coverage here. Verification also makes training roughly five to ten times slower. Since 3 D evaluation and additional seeds remain incomplete, we report a working training chain and partial evidence, not reproduction of the paper’s large headline gains.

title: Verifier semantics and protocol alignment
body: Observation consistency can differ from finite-GT membership
3D revision: valid structures confirmed 4→24 out of 26
Known gaps: training scale, epoch, N=4, and vote denominator
Undisclosed details are a question, not an established cause
notes: Verification introduces a second boundary. Some Boolean expressions satisfy observations but fall outside the finite reference grammar. In 3 D, revising representation and parsing increased confirmed valid structures from 4 to 24 out of 26, on the same observed training candidates. That is a diagnostic repair, not independent generalization. The paper publicly provides major settings; our teammate’s training scale, epoch 10 checkpoint, N 4 evaluation, and fixed voting denominator already differ from the paper or current code. We should align these before attributing the reproduction gap to missing details. SpeakerC will now explain why we moved from rewards to process distillation.
source: MS-TTRL AppendixB/C and official README; teammate stage report

title: Short explanations exposed a validity trade-off
body: 96 families/288 QA; 72 updates per SFT arm
Teacher content targets, not full reasoning traces
Hypothesis: shorter targets suppress useful checks
notes: We first compared answer-only supervision with short teacher explanations. Using 96 families and 288 QA pairs, we trained each arm for 72 updates. Outputs shrank from over five thousand tokens to tens or hundreds, but validity fell sharply and recovery did not improve. Shortness was clearly insufficient. The targets were teacher content, not full reasoning traces. Our trace audit also found repeated confirmations, incorrect deductions, and a bias toward simple answers. This motivated editing the student’s own reasoning rather than simply teaching a jump to the final answer.
source: DeepSeek-R1 distillation motivation https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948 ; E08/E09; short-target design is custom

title: DRP-inspired multi-outcome process distillation
body: Student traces → teacher editing → mechanism checks → SFT
Initial DRP attempt failed validity/coverage gates
Nine-arm diagnosis separates process type and ending weights
Selected: 48 families, 144 QA, 72 updates, LR 2e-5, end weight 3
notes: DRP suggests editing student reasoning before distillation. We adapted that idea with mechanism checks and targeted multi-outcome augmentation. The first attempt shortened outputs but harmed both validity and coverage. We then examined NF 4 versus BF 16 deployment, and compared four process types with two ending-token weights, plus an answer-only control. A 12-task development screen selected diverse_w. The selected model uses 48 families, 144 QA pairs, 72 updates, and a threefold weight on end-of-thinking and EOS tokens. This combines editing, repair, and augmentation; we cannot attribute the eventual result exclusively to pruning sentences.

title: Primary result: 27.5% fewer tokens; positive RR signal
body: Length reduction is supported; RR improvement is unconfirmed
notes: This is our primary result. The checkpoint was selected before freezing 36 unseen task families, with four samples per task. At the 8, 192-token cap, recovery rises from 15.57 to 18.28, and mean output falls from 5, 303 to 3, 846, a 27.5 percent reduction. The token-difference interval lies clearly below zero. The RR interval crosses zero, and its adjusted p-value is 0.258, so we call it a positive coverage signal, not a significant improvement. In 3 D, validity improves while coverage is unchanged, again separating validity from diversity. SpeakerD will explain the longer-budget and larger-scale follow-up.
source: E16 results/e16/summary.json; token intervals are unadjusted secondary analyses

title: More budget and data did not ensure more coverage
body: E16 at 40K: RR remains unconfirmed; no extra valid method samples
Expansion does not beat the old 48-family checkpoint
High LR can create wrong short answers or 40K reasoning tails
notes: At 40, 960 tokens, E 16 still saves 23.9 percent, but its RR advantage becomes smaller and remains unconfirmed. We also scanned learning rate and answer weighting, and expanded to 192 families, three training seeds, and 96 new held-out tasks. The expanded mean is slightly above Base, but not significant after correction, and does not exceed the earlier 48-family model. At 40 K, its token savings almost disappear. Aggressive learning rates produced either empty reasoning with wrong answers or very long incorrect traces. More updates, data, and tokens are not automatic gains. Rows here are within-experiment comparisons, not a cross-dataset ranking.

title: Valid mass, outcome concentration, and sample cost
body: IID model: E[RR@N]=(1/L) Σₖ[1−(1−pₖ)ᴺ]
Validity: mass inside GT; coverage: mass across different mechanisms
Rewards reshape support; multi-outcome targets may expand it
Shortening one answer’s trace does not create new mechanisms
notes: A simple IID model helps explain the results. If a mechanism has generation probability p, its chance of appearing at least once inN samples is one minus one minus p raised toN. Coverage depends both on valid probability mass and its concentration across outcomes. Frequency rewards reweight observed support; multi-outcome targets may expand it; process editing reduces sample cost. These are different operations. Self-verification can also amplify wrong cached labels. The formula explains later independent sampling, not the original history-conditioned loop. The next useful experiment should match total token or time cost, rather than assume shorter output automatically improves recovery.
source: Our probabilistic analysis under IID; MS-TTRL frequency-conflict motivation

title: Conclusions and reproducible outputs
body: Positive evidence: list-task reward mechanism; E16 output reduction
Boundaries: transfer, short targets, high LR, and scale remain constrained
Release: frozen tasks, raw token traces, scores, and CPU verification
Next: equal-cost sampling and orthogonal process/target controls
notes: Our contribution is an auditable chain of experiments. Group-aware rewards work on lists; E 16 clearly compresses outputs and gives a positive but unconfirmed coverage signal. Direct transfer, short explanations, and expansion do not establish stable coverage gains. The repository includes frozen tasks, raw token trajectories, task-level scores, and CPU verification. Next, we should spend saved tokens on extra sampling and independently vary process editing and multi-outcome targets. The unsuccessful attempts are useful because they identify which assumptions do not hold under our tested configurations.
